title: Gary Neville’s The Overlap buys Mark Goldbridge’s YouTube channels
content:
Gary Neville’s media company, The Overlap, has acquired the YouTube channels of online personality Mark Goldbridge.

The former Manchester United defender has struck a deal worth an undisclosed seven-figure sum to partner with Goldbridge, whose channels The United Stand and That’s Football boast 2.26 million and 1.46m subscribers respectively.

In a release on Tuesday, Neville said that the deal was designed to build “one of the most exciting independent football communities in the world”.

“The United Stand and That’s Football are two of the best-known football channels on YouTube, and our intention is to develop them into the most compelling Manchester United and football news channels in the market,” he added.

Goldbridge will continue to present on the channels but The Overlap’s acquisition will see new United-focused programming, including ‘Stick to United’, featuring former players and journalists, and ‘The Daily United’.

The 47-year-old, whose real name is Brent di Cesare, launched The United Stand in 2014 and has since gained both popularity and notoriety online through his reactions and rants to United’s performances.

Goldbridge said that he wants to “make The United Stand and That’s Football the best football channels in the world — not fan channels, the best football channels”.

“It’s not about money. This is about excitement. This is about what’s best for the community,” Goldbridge said in a live stream announcing the acquisition.

“For the last four years, I’ve felt there’s an issue with wanting to be the best community, but also running a business. We were looking for expansion. We were looking for a partner to take this whole thing forward. The Overlap were doing the same thing.”

Last year, Goldbridge’s channel won live broadcasting rights to stream Bundesliga games, the first deal of its kind between a major European football league and a UK-based YouTube content creator.

Neville set up The Overlap, his own YouTube channel, in 2021, with a roster of programming including Fan Debate and Stick to Football, a popular podcast alongside fellow pundits Jamie Carragher, Roy Keane, Jill Scott and Ian Wright.

Earlier this year, UK-based media company Global Media & Entertainment announced the acquisition of a majority stake in The Overlap. The channel has 1.66m subscribers on YouTube.
